posts.title: Three knots for the breakwater
posts.excerpt: The only three knots you need for a float rig, tied with cold fingers.
posts.content:
An improved clinch for the hook, a double uni to join line and leader, and a loop for the float stop. That is all.

Practise them at home on a pencil; at dawn on the wall there is no time to think.

posts.title: Sea bass on the turn of the tide
posts.excerpt: Why the half hour after high tide at the river mouth is worth an early alarm.
posts.content:
When the water starts to fall, small fish are pulled out of the reeds and the bass wait for them at the edge of the current.

A slim silver minnow, cast across and let it swing. Keep the rod low and the line tight.

posts.title: Low tide on the rocks
posts.excerpt: A safe first morning on the rocky shore: where to stand and what to bring.
posts.content:
Go out on a falling tide, stand on dry dark rock, never on the green weed, and keep the sea in front of you.

Bring a net, spare sinkers and a bucket of sea water for anything you plan to let go.
